header.userPrompt:
# Break up BankStatementReviewPage into smaller, readable components

## Problem

`web/src/main/scala/net/wiringbits/components/pages/BankStatementReviewPage.scala`
has grown to ~1100 lines in two large objects:

- `BankStatementReviewPage` — the route entry, plus ~20 pure helpers
  (`ResolvedImport`/`resolveImport`, `RowInfo`/`rowInfo`, `LinkedCategory`,
  `RowMenuItem`/`menuItemsFor`, `PrimaryAction`/`primaryActionFor`,
  `BulkRowDecision`/`bulkRowDecision`, `expenseMatches`, `resultLabel`,
  `statementMetadataLine`, `suggestionsPending`, `canRegenerateSuggestions`,
  summaries, …), the `ReviewData` model and its parallel `fetch`, and the outer
  `AsyncComponent`.
- `BankStatementReviewContent` — one ~700-line component holding all state, the
  action handlers (`handleIgnore`, `handleUnignore`, `handleUnlink`,
  `handleUnlinkRefund`, `handleBulkIgnore`, `handleBulkImport`,
  `handleRegenerateSuggestions`, `refreshRow`, `refreshExpenses`, drawer control)
  and a large render covering the header, the AI-suggestions controls, the
  filter + bulk-action toolbar, the rows table, and a drawer that hosts four
  different forms (create expense, create refund, link-to-existing-expense
  picker, create rule).

It is hard to read and navigate. Break it into cohesive, individually readable
pieces. **This is a pure refactor — no behaviour, API, or styling changes.**

## What to do

Split the file into focused units, each small enough to read on its own. A
reasonable shape (the exact boundaries are the implementer's call, as long as
the result is clearly smaller and cohesive):

- **A pure view-model / logic unit** (no React): the row resolution and
  classification helpers — `ResolvedImport`/`resolveImport`, `RowInfo`/`rowInfo`,
  `LinkedCategory`/`linkedCategoryDisplay`/`linkedMerchantName`, `RowMenuItem`/
  `menuItemsFor`, `PrimaryAction`/`primaryActionFor`, `BulkRowDecision`/
  `bulkRowDecision`, `expenseMatches`, the label/summary/suggestion helpers.
  These are already unit-tested (`BankStatementReviewPageSpec`) — keep the tests
  pointing at the new home.
- **The data loader** — `ReviewData` + its parallel `fetch` + the outer
  `AsyncComponent` wrapper that renders the content.
- **The content broken into sub-components**, each its own component/file, wired
  by a slim parent that owns the shared state and passes data + callbacks down:
  - the statement header + AI-suggestions controls (regenerate / polling status),
  - the filter + bulk-action toolbar (selection, Process / Ignore, progress,
    result summary),
  - the rows table/list (rendering `BankStatementReviewRow` per row),
  - the action drawer, ideally with each of its four forms as its own component.
- Keep `BankStatementReviewRow` as the per-row component (already separate); move
  more row presentation into it if that shrinks the parent.

## Constraints

- **Behaviour-preserving**: identical UI, data flow, and API calls. No endpoint,
  model, or evolution changes. The full existing behaviour (confirm, ignore,
  refund, manual link, rule creation, bulk process with link-or-create, AI-
  suggestion polling, drawer, toasts, filters) must be unchanged.
- Follow the project's frontend conventions (see `.orca/reviewers/frontend.md`
  and the self-check in `CLAUDE.md`): `FunctionalComponent` + `Props` per
  component; object-level `val`s hold only plain JS literals (no
  `KeyAddingStage`/`ReactElement`); use `def` for React elements reused in a
  render tree; MUI callbacks read Scala case classes via `(opt: Any) match`, not
  `js.Dynamic`; new views stay reachable (the parent composes them).
- Every extracted component is used by the parent — no dead components.
- Tests stay green and move with the code they cover; `web/Test/compile` must
  pass. Prefer keeping/By extending the existing page/row specs over deleting
  them.

## Out of scope

- No functional change to matching (`ReconciliationMatcher`), the bulk
  link-or-create logic, or any server code.
- No restyling or copy changes.

## Acceptance

- `BankStatementReviewPage.scala` is no longer a monolith: the pure helpers, the
  loader, and the content's major regions live in their own small, named
  components/files, each readable on its own.
- The app builds (`web/Test/compile`) and all existing web tests pass; the page
  behaves exactly as before.

tasks.title: Extract the pure review logic into BankStatementReviewLogic and move its spec
tasks.description:
Create `web/src/main/scala/net/wiringbits/components/pages/BankStatementReviewLogic.scala` (an `object BankStatementReviewLogic` with no React or MUI imports). Move these members out of `BankStatementReviewPage` into it verbatim, keeping their doc comments:
- `ResolvedImport`, both `resolveImport` overloads, `RowInfo`, `rowInfo`
- `LinkedCategory`, `linkedCategoryDisplay`, `linkedMerchantName`
- `RowMenuItem`, `menuItemsFor`, `PrimaryAction`, `primaryActionFor`
- `BulkRowDecision`, the private `manualLinkHint`, `bulkRowDecision`, `expenseMatches`, `bulkImportSummary`
- `resultLabel`, `suggestionsPending`, `canRegenerateSuggestions`

Also add two pure helpers that reproduce the inline content logic exactly:
- `filterRows(rows: List[GetBankStatement.StatementRowData], filter: String, rowInfoById: Map[UUID, RowInfo]): List[StatementRowData]`. Its cases are "ignored", "linked", "ready" (rows whose `rowInfoById.get(id).exists(_.isReady)`), "all", and default = unprocessed.
- `TabCounts(ready, unprocessed, ignored, linked, all)` + `tabCounts(rows, rowInfoById): TabCounts`.

Make `BankStatementReviewContent` use `filterRows`/`tabCounts` in place of its inline `filteredRows`/`countX` code. Leave `statementMetadataLine` (it returns a ReactElement) in place for now; a later task moves it into the header.

Update the imports in `BankStatementReviewPage.scala` (the content's `import BankStatementReviewPage.*` must now also import the logic object), in `BankStatementReviewRow.scala` and in `BankStatementReviewRowSpec.scala`.

Rename `web/src/test/scala/.../pages/BankStatementReviewPageSpec.scala` to `BankStatementReviewLogicSpec.scala` (class `BankStatementReviewLogicSpec`). Repoint every `BankStatementReviewPage.x` reference to `BankStatementReviewLogic.x`, and change the `"BankStatementReviewPage.resultLabel"` subject to `"resultLabel"` (per RULE-TE-001). Add `"filterRows"` and `"tabCounts"` cases that cover each tab. In `docs/guide/testing.md`, update the RULE-TE-010 example line from `BankStatementReviewPage.resultLabel` to `BankStatementReviewLogic.resultLabel`.

Verify with `CI=true sbt web/Test/compile` and `sbt "web/testOnly *BankStatementReviewLogicSpec *BankStatementReviewRowSpec"`.

tasks.title: Split BankStatementReviewContent into its own file; leave the page as the loader
Extract the header and filter tabs into components
tasks.description:
1. Create `BankStatementReviewHeader.scala`.
   - Props: `statement: GetBankStatement.Response`, `rowCount: Int`, `regenerateDisabled: Boolean`, `onRegenerate: () => Unit`.
   - It calls `useHistory()` for the Auto-reconcile and ← Back buttons.
   - It renders a `Fragment` holding the title row Box (filename, "N transactions", spacer, Regenerate AI suggestions/Regenerating…, Auto-reconcile, ← Back) and the metadata line.
   - Move `statementMetadataLine` out of `BankStatementReviewPage` into this object as a private `def`.
2. Create `BankStatementReviewTabs.scala`.
   - Props: `rowFilter: String`, `counts: BankStatementReviewLogic.TabCounts`, `onChange: String => Unit`.
   - It renders the same `mui.Tabs` with the same values, labels and sx.
   - Read the tab value with `MuiCompat.tabValue(v)` instead of `v.asInstanceOf[String]` (RULE-FE-014). This is equivalent because tab values are always strings.
3. In `BankStatementReviewContent`:
   - Keep the outer `padding 20px 24px 0 24px` Box and put `BankStatementReviewHeader(...)` and `BankStatementReviewTabs(...)` inside it, so the DOM is unchanged.
   - Pass `onRegenerate = () => handleRegenerateSuggestions(stmt.id)`.
   - Make the tab `onChange` a local `def` in the parent that does setRowFilter, then clears the selection, then `history.replace(s"$pathname?tab=$tab")`, as before.
   - The polling effect and the `regenerateSuggestionsDisabled`/`pollingSuggestions` computation stay in the parent.

No new DOM tests (RULE-TE-010). Verify with `CI=true sbt web/Test/compile` and the review specs.

tasks.title: Extract the bulk-action bar and bulk results list into components
tasks.description:
1. Create `BankStatementReviewBulkBar.scala`.
   - Props: `selectedCount: Int`, `bulkActive: Boolean`, `importProgress: BulkProgress`, `ignoreProgress: BulkProgress`, `onProcess: () => Unit`, `onIgnore: () => Unit`, `onClear: () => Unit`.
   - Use the type aliases from `BankStatementReviewPage`, or `Option[(Int, Int, Int)]`.
   - It renders exactly the current brand-coloured Box: the "N selected" label, a spacer, the Processing done/total (failed)… label or the "Process ready" button, the Ignoring… label or the "Ignore" button, and the × IconButton.
   - Show/hide stays in the parent (`if (selectedInView.nonEmpty) BulkBar(...) else Fragment()`).
2. Create `BankStatementReviewBulkResults.scala`.
   - Props: `results: List[(UUID, Either[String, Unit])]` (import results ++ ignore results, in that order) and `descById: Map[UUID, String]`.
   - It renders the `marginTop 16px` Box with one keyed Typography per result, using `BankStatementReviewLogic.resultLabel`. Success uses `var(--lc-success-text)`, failure `var(--lc-error)`.
   - The parent still decides to render it only when either results list is non-empty.
   - Keep `.withKey(rowId.toString)` on each mapped element.
3. Wire both into `BankStatementReviewContent` in the same positions (the bar before the error Box; the results inside the table scroll Box after the Table). Pass `onProcess = () => handleBulkImport(stmt.id, selectedInView.toList)` and the Ignore equivalent.

Verify with `CI=true sbt web/Test/compile` and the review specs.

tasks.title: Extract the rows table into BankStatementReviewTable
tasks.description:
Create `BankStatementReviewTable.scala` that renders the `mui.Table.size("small")`.

Props:
- `rows: List[StatementRowData]`, the already filtered rows
- `rowInfoById: Map[UUID, RowInfo]`
- `selectedRowIds: Set[UUID]`
- `showCheckbox: Boolean`, true for the unprocessed/ready filters
- `pollingSuggestions: Boolean`
- `expenseMatchById: Map[UUID, ReconciliationMatcher.ProposedAction]`
- `onSelectAll: Boolean => Unit`
- `onToggleSelected: (UUID, Boolean) => Unit`
- `onRowAction: (UUID, RowAction) => Unit`

What it renders:
- A head row: the select-all checkbox (allSelected/indeterminate computed inside from rows + selection), then the Date / Amount / Description / Category / Match / blank header cells.
- A body that is either the "No transactions in this view." colSpan 7 row, or `BankStatementReviewRow` per row with `.withKey(row.id.toString)`.
- `linksToExpense` is computed as before (AutoLink → true).
- `hcell` may become a private object-level `val` (`CSSPropertiesUtils` is a plain JS literal, which RULE-FE-002 allows).

In the parent:
- Keep the scroll Box and render `BankStatementReviewTable(...)` followed by the bulk results.
- `onSelectAll = checked => if (checked) setSelectedRowIds(tableRows.map(_.id).toSet) else setSelectedRowIds(Set.empty)`.
- Pass the existing stable `onToggleSelected`/`onRowAction` `useCallback` values unchanged, so the memoised rows keep skipping re-renders.
- Remove the now-unused `allTableSelected`/`someTableSelected`/`hcell` from the parent.

Verify with `CI=true sbt web/Test/compile` and the review specs.

tasks.title: Extract the action drawer, its row summary and form dispatch
tasks.description:
1. Create `BankStatementReviewDrawer.scala`. Its object holds `enum DrawerForm { case CreateExpense, CreateRefund, LinkExpense, CreateRule }`.
2. Add a pure helper `activeForm(creating: Option[UUID], refund: Option[UUID], linking: Option[UUID], rule: Option[UUID]): Option[(UUID, DrawerForm)]`.
   - It returns the first defined of creating → refund → linking → rule.
   - This matches the old precedence: `drawerRowId` is creating.orElse(refund).orElse(linking).orElse(rule), and the forms were checked in the same order.
3. Drawer Props:
   - `ctx`, `stmtId`, `open: Boolean`, `target: Option[(GetBankStatement.StatementRowData, DrawerForm)]`
   - `merchants`, `categories`, `ruleList: List[ImportRuleMatcher.Rule]` (the explicit rules, not the effective ones, as today), `aiSuggestions: Option[AiSuggestions]`
   - `onClose: () => Unit`, `onCancel: DrawerForm => Unit`
   - `onExpenseCreated: (UUID, UUID) => Unit`, `onRefundCreated: (UUID, UUID) => Unit`, `onExpenseLinked: (UUID, UUID) => Unit`
   - `onRuleCreated: (ImportRuleMatcher.Rule, Option[GetMerchants.Response.Merchant]) => Unit`
   - `onNewEntities`, with the same signature as `BankRowCreateExpenseForm.Props.onNewEntities`
4. The drawer renders the same `mui.Drawer.anchor("right")`: a 480px Box, the "Review transaction" header with the × button (onClose), then, when a target exists, the row summary plus the matching existing form component.
   - Pass each form the same props as today. `aiSuggestion = aiSuggestions.flatMap(_.rows.find(_.rowId == row.id))` stays as is (it does not filter on Done).
   - Use `.fold[ReactElement](Fragment())` (RULE-FE-016).
5. Create `BankStatementRowSummary.scala`: a small component with Props `row: StatementRowData` that renders the "From statement" card (description, date, signed coloured amount) exactly as before.
6. In `BankStatementReviewContent`:
   - Keep the four `Option[UUID]` states and `onRowAction` unchanged.
   - Compute `target` from `activeForm` + `statementRows.find`.
   - Map `onCancel` to the specific setter (`CreateExpense` → `setCreatingForRow(None)`, etc.). The old per-form cancel cleared only its own state; `onClose` keeps `closeDrawer()` clearing all four.
   - Move the old success lambdas, including their toasts, verbatim into the parent callbacks. Expense created: patch expenseId, close the form, `refreshRow`, toast "Expense created". Refund: patch refundId, close, toast "Refund created". Link: patch expenseId, close, `refreshRow`, no toast. Rule: append the rule, and the merchant if present, then close and toast "Rule created".
7. Add a pure `BankStatementReviewDrawerSpec` covering `activeForm` precedence and None.

Verify with `CI=true sbt web/Test/compile` and `sbt "web/testOnly *BankStatementReviewDrawerSpec *BankStatementReviewLogicSpec *BankStatementReviewRowSpec"`.

tasks.title: Move the bulk ignore/import runs out of the content component
tasks.description:
Create `BankStatementBulkRuns.scala`, a non-React object. Move `handleBulkIgnore` and `handleBulkImport` into it as plain functions that take explicit parameters rather than closing over component state.

Parameters:
- `client` (`ctx.api.client`) and an implicit `ExecutionContext`
- `stmtId`, `ids: List[UUID]`
- for import, the render-time snapshots `statementRows`, `rowInfoById`, `expenseMatchById` and `expenseList`
- `setStatementRows`, `setProgress`, `setResults`, `setSelectedRowIds` (`SetStateHookCallback`s or `(A => A) => Unit` / `A => Unit` functions)
- `showToast` and `onRefresh`, for import

The bodies must stay identical:
- the sequential `loop` and the `Counts` case class
- `bulkRowDecision` dispatch to ignoreRow / linkRowToExpense / createExpenseFromRow
- the same row patches: ignoredAt = now; expenseId, merchantId and single-split categoryId on link; expenseId, res.merchantId and res.categoryId on create
- the same progress tuples and result entries
- `linkedThisRun` tracking
- at the end of an import: clear progress, clear selection, toast with `bulkImportSummary(...)`, then `onRefresh()`
- at the end of an ignore: clear progress and selection only

Keep the comment about matches coming from this render. `BankStatementReviewContent` then calls these with its current state and the hoisted progress/results setters from props. The single-row handlers (ignore, unignore, unlink, unlinkRefund, regenerate, refreshRow, refreshExpenses) stay in the parent.

Afterwards, check that the parent reads as state + polling effect + memos + single-row handlers + composition, and is a few hundred lines at most. Verify with `CI=true sbt web/Test/compile` and the review specs.

resultJson.brief:
Module and location
- Frontend only. Scala.js + Slinky 0.7 + React 18 + MUI 5 via ScalablyTyped (`com.olvind.mui.muiMaterial.components as mui`).
- Package `net.wiringbits.components.pages` under `web/src/main/scala/net/wiringbits/components/pages/`. Tests mirror it under `web/src/test/scala/net/wiringbits/components/pages/`.
- Keep every new file in this package; the existing drawer forms live here too.

Files involved
- `BankStatementReviewPage.scala`, the file being split.
  - L41-381: `object BankStatementReviewPage`. Holds pure helpers, `ReviewData`, the type aliases `RowEdits = Map[UUID,(String,String,String)]`, `BulkProgress = Option[(Int,Int,Int)]` (done,total,failed) and `BulkResults = List[(UUID, Either[String, Unit])]`, and the route component.
  - The route component: parses `useParams().get("stmtId")`; fires 5 futures in parallel (getBankStatement, getMerchants, getCategories, getImportRules mapped via `ImportRuleMatcher.Rule.fromApi`, getExpenses); hoists the toast and bulk progress/results state above the remount; renders `AsyncComponent[ReviewData](fetch, render = BankStatementReviewContent(...).withKey(timesRefreshing.toString), progressIndicator = () => Loader(ctx), watchedObjects = List(timesRefreshing))` plus a Snackbar.
  - L386-1094: `object BankStatementReviewContent`, which does `import BankStatementReviewPage.*`.
- `BankStatementReviewRow.scala`: per-row component, wrapped in `React.memo(..., (prev, next) => prev == next)`.
  - It defines `enum RowAction { OpenExpenseForm, OpenRefundForm, OpenLinkPicker, OpenRuleForm, Ignore, Unignore, Unlink, UnlinkRefund }`.
  - Props: `row`, `info: RowInfo`, `selected`, `showCheckbox`, `pollingSuggestions`, `linksToExpense`, `onToggleSelected: (UUID, Boolean) => Unit`, `onAction: (UUID, RowAction) => Unit`.
  - It imports `LinkedCategory`, `PrimaryAction`, `RowInfo`, `RowMenuItem`, `menuItemsFor` and `primaryActionFor` from `BankStatementReviewPage`; these must be repointed.
- Existing drawer forms (do not change their APIs):
  - `BankRowCreateExpenseForm.Props(stmtId, row, merchants, categories, ruleList, aiSuggestion: Option[AiSuggestions.RowSuggestion], ctx, onSuccess: UUID => Unit, onCancel, onNewEntities: (Option[Rule], Option[Merchant]) => Unit)`
  - `BankRowCreateRefundForm.Props(stmtId, rowId, row, merchants, categories, ruleList, ctx, onSuccess: UUID => Unit, onCancel)`
  - `BankRowLinkPicker.Props(stmtId, rowId, ctx, onSuccess: UUID => Unit, onCancel)`
  - `BankRowRuleForm.Props(stmtId, row, merchants, categories, ctx, onSuccess: (Rule, Option[Merchant]) => Unit, onCancel)`
  - Read their files for exact types.
- Tests:
  - `BankStatementReviewPageSpec.scala` is a pure AnyWordSpec over the helpers.
  - `BankStatementReviewRowSpec.scala` is a jsdom render test that imports `LinkedCategory`, `ResolvedImport` and `RowInfo` from `BankStatementReviewPage`.
  - `BankRowCreateExpenseFormSpec` is unaffected.
- `AppRouter.scala:95` routes `/bank-statements/:stmtId` to `BankStatementReviewPage(props.ctx, user)`. Keep that entry point.
- `docs/guide/testing.md` RULE-TE-010 cites `BankStatementReviewPage.resultLabel` as an example.

Key APIs
- Models are in `net.wiringbits.api.models.*`:
  - `GetBankStatement.Response`: id, documentFilename, bankName, productType, currency, accountLast4, periodStart, periodEnd, statementRows, aiSuggestions: Option[AiSuggestions].
  - `GetBankStatement.StatementRowData`: id, date, amount: BigDecimal, description, txnType, expenseId, refundId, ignoredAt, expenseMerchantId, expenseCategoryId, …
  - `AiSuggestions(status: AiSuggestionsStatus, model, rows: List[RowSuggestion(rowId, categoryId, merchantId)])`
  - `GetMerchants.Response.Merchant`, `GetCategories.Response.Category`, `GetExpenses.Response.Expense` (with `splits`, `merchantId`)
- `net.wiringbits.api.utils.{ImportRuleMatcher, RowRuleVerdict}`: `ImportRuleMatcher.effectiveRules(rules, merchants.map(m => m.id -> m.name))`, `RowRuleVerdict.verdict(rules, description)`.
- `net.wiringbits.utils.ReconciliationMatcher`: `unlinkedByDate`, `candidatesFor`, `matchRow`, and `ProposedAction` = AutoLink(id) | NeedsReview(ids) | CreateNew.
- API client methods (`props.ctx.api.client`), all Futures handled with `.onComplete`: getBankStatement, getExpenses, ignoreRow, unignoreRow, unlinkRow, unlinkRowRefund, linkRowToExpense(stmtId, rowId, LinkRowToExpense.Request(expenseId)), createExpenseFromRow(stmtId, rowId, CreateExpenseFromRow.Request(...)), regenerateBankStatementAiSuggestions.
- Router: `useHistory()`, `RouterCompat.useTypedLocation()`, `URLSearchParams` (from `org.scalajs.dom`). `MuiCompat.tabValue(v: Any): String` is in `net.wiringbits.webapp.utils.slinkyUtils.compat.MuiCompat`.

Conventions (docs/guide/frontend.md, antipatterns.md, CLAUDE.md self-check)
- Component shape: `object X { def apply(props: Props): KeyAddingStage = component(props); case class Props(...); val component: FunctionalComponent[Props] = FunctionalComponent[Props] { props => ... } }`. That is the style already used by Content and Row. Pass `AppContext` via Props, never via useContext.
- Object-level `val`s may only hold plain JS literals (`new CSSPropertiesUtils {...}`), never `KeyAddingStage` or `ReactElement`. Use `def` for elements created more than once in a render.
- Use `.fold[ReactElement](Fragment())` for Option rendering, and put `.withKey` on every mapped element.
- No `js.Dynamic` or `asInstanceOf` in new component code; use the compat helpers.
- MUI builders often need the `(x.build: ReactElement)` or `(x: ReactElement)` ascription inside if/else and match branches, as the existing code does.
- Tests: `"methodName" should { "behaviour" in ... }`, never repeating the class name. Prefer pure-function unit tests. DOM tests are added only to guard a known crash (RULE-TE-010); if one is added, use jsdom + `BrowserRouter` for components that call useHistory.
- Build: `CI=true` enables -Werror, so remove unused imports in every file you touch. Typecheck with `CI=true sbt web/Test/compile`. Run targeted specs with `sbt "web/testOnly *Spec1 *Spec2"`, never the full suite. Run `sbt scalafmtAll` before finishing. Web tests need Node 24 on PATH (the default shell node is v16, and yarn install fails on it).

Behaviour invariants to preserve (non-obvious)
- Toast and bulk progress/results live in the page because a refresh remounts Content via `withKey(timesRefreshing)`. State seeded from `data` inside Content is therefore always fresh. Bulk import ends with `props.onRefresh()`, which causes that remount.
- `onToggleSelected` (deps `""`) and `onRowAction` (deps `List(stmtId.toString)`) are `Hooks.useCallback` values that the memoised rows depend on. Pass them through untouched, and don't wrap them in new lambdas on the way down.
- The polling effect uses `js.Array(suggestionsPollKey)` deps with key `s"$stmtId:$pollingSuggestions"`, max 20 attempts at 3000 ms. This conflicts with RULE-FE-006 but is existing behaviour; keep it as is (moving it verbatim is fine).
- Memo chain: `effectiveRuleList` (ruleList, merchantList) → `rowInfoById` → `unlinkedExpensesByDate` (expenseList) → `expenseMatchById`. Keep the same deps.
- Drawer:
  - `drawerOpen` is true when any of the four Option[UUID] states is set. `closeDrawer` clears all four; each form's onCancel clears only its own state.
  - `OpenExpenseForm` also clears linking, and `OpenLinkPicker` also clears creating.
  - Refund and Rule success don't call `refreshRow`; Expense and Link success do. Link success shows no toast.
- The rule list passed to the forms is the explicit `ruleList`, not `effectiveRuleList`.
- The tab filter default is \"ready\" when `?tab` is absent. A tab change sets the filter, clears the selection and does `history.replace(s\"$pathname?tab=$tab\")`. The select-all and row checkboxes appear only for the \"unprocessed\" and \"ready\" filters.
- `bulkActive` = selectedInView.nonEmpty && no bulk progress running. `selectedInView` = the selection intersected with the filtered row ids.
- Dead code in Content: `rowEdits`/`setRowEdits` state and the imports `ConfirmBankStatementRow`, `IgnoreRow`, `UnignoreRow`. Unused imports may be dropped as part of the move; leave the dead `rowEdits` state in place and mention it in the summary rather than deleting it.

entries.resultJson:
The full suite passes. `CI=true NODE_OPTIONS=--openssl-legacy-provider sbt test` exited with code 0 on the first run, so I didn't need to fix anything.

- **Setup:** I used Node v24 from nvm. Postgres was already running in Docker, so I didn't have to start it.
- **Results:** no failures in any module. The modules reported 36, 56, 36, 56, 859 and 286 passing tests; 286 is the web module.
- **Log noise:** the log has `error` and `Failed` lines, but they are expected. They come from tests that deliberately trigger failures, such as `BackgroundJobTypeRunnerSpec`'s "claim boom" and "record boom", and from test names containing "Failed". There is also one harmless MUI `anchorEl` prop-type warning from jsdom.

resultJson.title: Split BankStatementReviewPage into smaller components
resultJson.body:
`BankStatementReviewPage.scala` was about 1,100 lines: one object full of helpers and one content component of about 700 lines. This PR splits it into small files in the same package. It is meant as a pure refactor, with no changes to behaviour, API, styling or copy.

- **`BankStatementReviewLogic`**: the pure helpers with no React (row resolution and classification, bulk decisions, expense matching, labels, suggestion checks). It also holds `ReviewData` and the type aliases, plus a new `filterRows` that replaces the inline tab filter. The existing spec now points here (`BankStatementReviewLogicSpec`), and the example in `docs/guide/testing.md` is updated to match.
- **`BankStatementReviewPage`**: now only the route entry, the parallel fetch, the toast and bulk state kept above the remount, and the `AsyncComponent` wrapper.
- **`BankStatementReviewContent`**: a slimmer parent. It owns the shared state and memos and passes data and callbacks to new components: `BankStatementReviewHeader`, `BankStatementReviewTabs`, `BankStatementReviewBulkBar`, `BankStatementReviewTable`, `BankStatementReviewBulkResults` and `BankStatementReviewDrawer` (with `BankStatementRowSummary`). The drawer chooses its form with a pure `activeForm`, which keeps the old precedence: create, then refund, then link, then rule.
- **Handlers moved out of the component**: the bulk ignore and bulk import runs are now plain functions in `BankStatementBulkRuns`. The single-row actions and the AI-suggestion polling moved into `BankStatementRowActions` and `BankStatementSuggestionsPolling`.

Things to check in review:
- The parent still wraps the components in the same Boxes, so the rendered tree should not change.
- The stable `onToggleSelected` and `onRowAction` callbacks are passed to the memoised rows without being wrapped.
- The tab change handler now reads the tab value with `MuiCompat.tabValue` instead of `asInstanceOf[String]`.
- The `rowEdits` state was already dead code and is left in place on purpose.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)
